page: Microsoft Azure E32-16ds_v6 is an x86_64 architecture server instance belonging to the Edsv6 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical Intel Xeon 8573C cores with hyper-threading enabled. The processor operates at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz and includes a 260 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 256.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 16.0 GB per vCPU. The instance also includes 1890 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and is capable of utilizing Premium Storage. No GPUs are included in this configuration.

In benchmark evaluations, the E32-16ds_v6 demonstrates strong single-core performance, scoring 2112.0 in Geekbench single-core tests and 2701.0 in text processing, both placing in the top 25% tier. Multi-core performance is moderate, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 13078.0 and a Passmark CPU score of 26677.0. The hardware supports Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), which contribute to a text generation speed of 373.31 tokens/second for small 135M parameter LLM models, placing it in the top 10% tier for this metric. Memory read bandwidth reaches 1241.63 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 120.69 GB/sec for uncached large blocks.

Given its high memory density of 16 GB per vCPU and integrated 1890 GB NVMe SSD, the E32-16ds_v6 offers a resource-dense profile for memory-bound workloads without requiring the allocation of excess compute cores. This makes it a qualitatively cost-efficient choice for hosting large relational databases, in-memory caches like Redis, and data analytics pipelines. The absence of a dedicated GPU limits its utility for heavy deep learning training, but its AMX-enabled Intel Xeon processor provides capable CPU-based inference for smaller language models. It is highly suited for memory-intensive enterprise applications, database operations, and text processing tasks.
